context:
Goal: an agent's relative `../` write never lands outside its own checkout by mistake.
Problem (rule): one of the two incident agents was a reviewer working in its caller's checkout, so it had no recorded home, and your decision allows such an agent. Covering it changes your decision's sentence.
Based on (read): step guard-relative-write-escape: on 2026-11-08 an agent's relative `../` mkdir escaped its worktree twice (a #1458 test-author and an earlier reviewer) and made /home/user/tmp.
Based on (ruling): decision an-agent-outside-its-home-tree-must-stop (latest cited event 2026-10-27) allows an agent with no recorded home to write anywhere ("No record ... This part allows it.", line 24 on main, read 06:34 CST Nov 8). Asked again because a 2026-11-08 incident shows a reviewer with no recorded home writing outside its checkout, which that ruling did not weigh.
Departs from: main, where an agent with no recorded home may write anywhere — refuses that agent's relative shell write that lands outside the checkout holding its working folder.
Meanwhile: lane guard-relative-write-escape (session_013NEJKzJxDxuXzuwNe7fhYn) builds both parts, with the no-record part separable, and drops it on b.

options.gain: The reviewer form of the incident is closed, so a stray ../ write by a reviewer no longer lands in a shared tree.
options.how: The guard refuses a relative shell write by any agent, recorded home or not, when it lands outside the checkout that holds the agent's working folder. The decision's no-record sentence is rewritten in place.
options.label: Cover agents with no recorded home too
options.lose: A reviewer's deliberate relative write outside its checkout is refused (none seen).

options.how: The guard refuses the relative write only for an agent with a recorded home. The lane drops the no-record part.
options.label: Recorded homes only
options.lose: The reviewer form of the incident stays open.

ref: step guard-relative-write-escape; decision an-agent-outside-its-home-tree-must-stop (line 24 on main)
reply: You picked neither (10:05 CST Nov 8): both options lose something large. A third option is being shaped: give every agent a recorded home when it is spawned (a reviewer's home is its caller's checkout), so the guard covers the reviewer with no change to your decision's sentence. The lane guard-relative-write-escape checks it can be built, then it comes back as a new question. Routed to the coordinator and that lane (session_013NEJKzJxDxuXzuwNe7fhYn); home: step guard-relative-write-escape. Closed 10:09 CST Nov 8.
short: Relative ../ writes: cover agents with no home
title: Should the guard also refuse a relative ../ write outside its checkout by an agent with no recorded home?
